_: Shared behavioural table for the interest-parameter refusals — see scripts/check-mirrors.js check 15. `jayhind-client-back/src/const/interest.const.ts` enforces them; `jayhindi-client-front/src/utils/interest-rules.util.ts` states them in the per-ledger interest dialog so an operator reads the reason instead of meeting a 400. Both must answer every expanded row with the SAME SENTENCE, and both must match the sentence stated here — so a wording one side quietly improved, and a rule both sides forgot together, are different failures.
__notMirrored: ⚠️ Only the REFUSAL is mirrored, never the calculator. `interestOn`, `daysBetween` and the two day-count conventions live server-side alone: the Interest Report renders figures the server computed and the browser never recomputes one, so a second copy would be a rule with no reader. P8b-2 shipped exactly that (a `varianceVerdict` copy nothing called) and its own UI gate proved it by injecting a wrong verdict there and passing 6/6. A mirror exists so a screen does not OFFER what the server will refuse; a computed figure is not an offer.
__closedSet: The compounding interval is a CLOSED set of four, and it is closed because the refusal names them. The rule's first cut accepted any whole 1-12 while printing '1, 3, 6 or 12', so a stored 5 was legal and unmentionable — caught by the backend spec, and the vectors below keep it closed on both sides.

messages.negative: An interest rate cannot be negative — a ledger that should charge nothing has no interest parameters at all, rather than a rate below zero.
messages.typo: ${ratePercent}% a year is almost certainly a typo — interest is stated per annum, so 18 means 18% a year and not 18% a month.
messages.bad-style: "${style}" is not an interest style — it is either simple or compound.
messages.bad-basis: "${basis}" is not a day-count basis — it is either actual days over 365 or the 30-day-month convention.
messages.bad-grace: A grace period is a whole number of days, and cannot be negative.
messages.bad-interval: Compounding happens monthly, quarterly, half-yearly or yearly — 1, 3, 6 or 12 months apart.

terms.why: Well-formed, including a ZERO rate (a ledger that charges nothing but keeps its parameters) and the boundary 100.
All four intervals of the closed set.
⚠️ A stored interval a SIMPLE ledger does not use must not refuse the save — an operator switching compound → simple would otherwise be stuck with a value they cannot see.

⚠️ The sentence must say what to do INSTEAD — remove the parameters — because the operator's intent (charge nothing) has a different expression, and 'cannot be negative' alone leaves them looking for one.
⚠️ A TYPO GUARD that names the actual mistake — 18 meaning 18% a MONTH gives 216% a year — rather than implying a statutory ceiling exists.
An unknown style. The empty string is included because it is a STATED value, not an absent one.
An unknown basis. `actual-actual` and `30/360` are real finance conventions this app deliberately does not offer.
Whole days, never negative — grace moves the START, so a fractional or negative one has no meaning.
⚠️ A CLOSED set: 2, 5 and 7 are whole numbers of months and are still refused, because the sentence names four and the rule has to mean what it says.
